Definition: properly, a region across; but used only adverbially (with or without a preposition) on the opposite side (especially of the Jordan; ususally meaning the east)
BiblicalUsage: This word marks the other side, most often the far side of the Jordan, and it draws the map of Israel's story. Moses speaks to Israel beyond Jordan, the tribes settle on both sides of the river, and Solomon's kingdom stretches from beyond the river to the border of Egypt. The word is small, but it tells you where God's people stand and which way they are facing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God meets His people on both sides of every river, because no boundary keeps Him out. The far side is still His ground, and the crossing is still His doing.
